title: 从源头到河口：河流如何塑造大地
topic: How a river shapes the land, from mountain source to delta

sentences.en: So today I want to trace a single river all the way from its source high in the mountains down to the sea, because a river is really the best tool we have for reading a landscape.
sentences.zh: 那么今天，我想沿着一条河，从它在群山高处的源头一路追踪到大海，因为要读懂一片地貌，河流其实是我们手上最好的工具。

sentences.en: Most large rivers begin at high elevation, often on a plateau or in a glacier field, where the terrain is steep and the water moves fast.
sentences.zh: 多数大河都发源于海拔较高处，往往是在高原上，或者在冰川区域，那里地势陡峭，水流湍急。

sentences.en: At that altitude the land is cold, so as the glacier slowly melts, the meltwater starts cutting downhill, and this is where erosion really begins.
sentences.zh: 在那样的高度上，土地寒冷，所以当冰川缓慢消融时，融水便开始向下切割，而侵蚀正是从这里真正开始的。

sentences.en: Now, the high ground that separates one river system from the next is called a watershed—rain falling on one side of that ridge drains into our river, and rain on the other side goes somewhere else entirely.
sentences.zh: 那么，把一个水系和相邻水系分开的那道高地，就叫分水岭——落在这道山脊一侧的雨水汇入我们这条河，另一侧的雨水则完全流向别处。

sentences.en: As the river descends, smaller streams join it; each of these feeder streams is a tributary, and together they collect water from the whole surrounding region.
sentences.zh: 随着河流下降，更小的溪流汇入其中；这些注水的小溪每一条都是支流，它们共同从周围整片区域汇集来水。

sentences.en: The entire area that funnels water into one river is called its drainage basin, and a major river basin can cover an enormous stretch of land.
sentences.zh: 把水都汇集进同一条河的整片区域，被称为它的流域，而一个大型河流流域可以覆盖极其广阔的土地。

sentences.en: The shape of that basin depends heavily on the local topography—where the highlands sit, how the valleys run, and which way the whole surface tilts.
sentences.zh: 这个流域的形状在很大程度上取决于当地的地形——高地位于何处、河谷如何延伸、整个地表朝哪个方向倾斜。

sentences.en: Climate matters just as much, and climate depends partly on latitude: a river running through the tropical zone near the equator behaves very differently from one at high latitudes.
sentences.zh: 气候同样重要，而气候部分取决于纬度：一条穿过赤道附近热带地带的河流，与一条身处高纬度的河流，表现极为不同。

sentences.en: In many temperate zones the flow is fairly steady through the year, but in regions shaped by the monsoon, most of the water arrives in just a few months of heavy summer rain.
sentences.zh: 在许多温带地区，河流的水量全年相当稳定，但在受季风影响的区域，大部分水量只在夏季那几个月的暴雨中到来。

sentences.en: And in arid parts of the world, a river may be the only reliable water for hundreds of miles, which is exactly why early farmers built canals for irrigation and grew their crops right along its banks.
sentences.zh: 而在世界上的干旱地带，一条河可能是方圆几百英里内唯一可靠的水源，这正是为什么早期农民会修建水渠进行灌溉，并沿着河岸种植作物。

sentences.en: By the time the river reaches lower ground, it has slowed down and spread out across a broad, flat plain, and instead of cutting the land it now starts dropping the sediment it has carried.
sentences.zh: 等到河流抵达低地时，它已经放缓并铺展开来，漫过一片宽广平坦的平原，此时它不再切割土地，而是开始卸下一路携带的泥沙。

sentences.en: Where the river finally meets the ocean, all that sediment piles up into a fan-shaped delta, and because the soil there is so fresh and fertile, deltas have supported dense populations for thousands of years.
sentences.zh: 在河流最终汇入海洋之处，那些泥沙堆积成一片扇形的三角洲，而由于那里的土壤如此新鲜肥沃，三角洲数千年来一直养育着稠密的人口。

sentences.en: The delta also reshapes the coastline itself, pushing the boundary between land and sea slowly outward as more and more material settles.
sentences.zh: 三角洲还会重塑海岸线本身，随着越来越多的物质沉积下来，缓慢地把陆地与海洋之间的界线向外推移。

sentences.en: This is why so many great cities grew up on deltas and river mouths, and why river valleys still drive so much of the world's urbanization today.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么众多伟大的城市在三角洲和河口兴起，也是为什么直到今天，河谷仍在推动着世界上如此大规模的城市化。

sentences.en: A river will also carve out useful shapes at the coast—it can leave behind a narrow peninsula reaching into the water, or an isthmus of land that connects two larger pieces of ground.
sentences.zh: 河流在海岸处还会塑造出有用的形态——它可能留下一道伸入水中的狭长半岛，或者一条连接两大块陆地的地峡。

sentences.en: Early explorers who mapped these features advanced the science of cartography, and to fix any point precisely they needed both its latitude and its longitude.
sentences.zh: 那些测绘这些地貌的早期探险家推动了制图学的发展，而要精确定位任何一点，他们既需要它的纬度，也需要它的经度。

sentences.en: And keep in mind that the same river system can look completely different depending on which hemisphere it sits in, since the seasons in the north and south are flipped.
sentences.zh: 还要记住，同一个水系身处哪个半球，看上去可能截然不同，因为南北半球的季节是颠倒的。

sentences.en: So a river isn't just water moving downhill—it's a slow machine that carries the mountains, grain by grain, all the way down to the sea.
sentences.zh: 所以，河流不只是向下流动的水——它是一台缓慢的机器，把群山一粒接一粒地，一路搬运到大海里去。
